inputs.original_text: DSD athletes also face exclusion from future Olympics IOC says move will protect fairness and safety’ The International Olympic Committee has banned transgender women and DSD athletes from the female category of events at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games in a landmark decision. Kirsty Coventry, president of the IOC, said: “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category.” Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The IOC is presenting its ban on transgender women and DSD athletes from the female category at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games as a matter of “fairness and safety.” That sounds less like a neutral safeguard and more like a convenient justification for tightening control over who gets to compete—and for making a political decision look inevitable. When Kirsty Coventry says, “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category,” the certainty of the wording does the work: it closes down debate while the institution gets to define the terms. Don’t assume the official explanation tells you whose interests this decision really serves.
